clue.text: Further loan on security

definitions.meaning: to further a cause is to promote or push it forward
money lent up front, as against wages or collateral

explanation.surface: A borrower asks the bank for another loan secured against property.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: to promote something, and a sum of money lent before it is due.

clue.text: Stop after snake makes for pitch

indicators.note: the stopping word comes after the snake

parts.note: an asp is an Egyptian snake
halt means stop

explanation.surface: A cricket match is halted by a snake on the field.
explanation.walkthrough: Pitch looks like a sports ground, but here it is tar, the black road-surface material.
explanation.definitionFit: Pitch is a tarry bituminous substance, and road surfacing is made from such tar mixed with gravel.

clue.text: Profit from uranium found in valley

indicators.note: the chemical letter sits inside the word for valley

parts.note: a vale is a poetic word for a valley
U is the chemical symbol for uranium

explanation.surface: Prospectors make money from uranium deposits in a valley.
explanation.definitionFit: Benefit or worth gained from something, as in getting good return for money.

clue.text: Hotel in pleasant position

indicators.note: the radio letter goes inside the word for pleasant

parts.note: nice means pleasant
Hotel is H in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A hotel sits in an agreeable location.
explanation.definitionFit: A suitable place or role that one fits into neatly, such as a market slot.

clue.text: The ultimate consumer?

parts.note: ultimate suggests the greatest shopper, but it means the last in the chain: the person who finally uses a product

explanation.surface: A question about who might be the greatest shopper of all.
explanation.definitionFit: In commerce, the person at the end of the supply chain who actually puts a product to use.

clue.text: Gifted small son brought in milk

indicators.note: the two short letters are placed inside the word for milk

parts.note: to milk someone is to bleed them dry
S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A talented little boy is fetched to help with the dairy work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Milk' looks like a noun but is the verb to exploit, BLEED.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone blessed with a talent is endowed or favoured with it, so blessed works as a synonym.

clue.text: Moment one monster and knight seen in land?

parts.note: monster as an adjective means huge, big

indicators.note: the chess letter appears inside the word for land

parts.note: to land a fish or prize is to bag it
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: A huge beast and a knight appear at once in some realm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moment one' means the first instant, the start of the universe; land is a verb, not a country.
explanation.definitionFit: Cosmologists name the explosive origin of the universe as its first instant.

clue.text: Sent a snap to be developed, incidentally

indicators.note: a photograph is developed, and here the letters are processed into a new form

explanation.surface: Someone mentions in passing that a photo was sent off for developing.
explanation.definitionFit: A French phrase meaning in passing, used for something said by the way.

clue.text: Tiger seen abroad where lion holds sway?

indicators.note: abroad suggests scattering far and wide, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tiger spotted overseas, in a land where the lion is king.
explanation.definitionFit: This Tanzanian national park is famous savannah territory dominated by big cats.

clue.text: Carefully analyse underworld worshippers?

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld and the realm itself
a sect is a religious group

explanation.surface: Scholars study a cult that worships the god of the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: To examine something in minute detail, like cutting up a specimen, is to analyse it.

clue.text: Alsatian? Or poodle transformed with CGI?

indicators.note: the letters of the dog breed and the effects acronym are changed into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A film-maker wonders whether to use a real Alsatian or a computer-generated poodle.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks Alsatian as an example: the German shepherd is the classic breed used by the police.
explanation.definitionFit: German shepherds (Alsatians) are a typical example of a dog trained for police work.

clue.text: Church district not completely in capital

indicators.note: the final letter of the word for a church district is lopped off

parts.note: a parish is the area served by one church

explanation.surface: A church area lies partly within a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: The French capital city is the most familiar example of a capital.

clue.text: Young forever lacking regular income? Wife's gone

indicators.note: the wife's abbreviation has left, so that letter is removed

parts.note: with no weekly wage, so wageless

explanation.surface: A man without a salary laments that his wife has left him, though he still feels young.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wife's gone' reads as 'wife is gone': the 's is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that never seems to grow old stays youthful for ever, as in a timeless beauty.

clue.text: Scene changed after sailor gets leave

indicators.note: the sailor comes first and the shuffled scene follows it

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a common crossword sailor

indicators.note: the letters of scene are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: A theatre set is rearranged after a sailor is granted shore leave.
explanation.definitionFit: Time away from work granted to an employee, as in leave of absence, is a period off duty.

clue.text: Prescription for Verity?

parts.note: Verity looks like a woman's name, but it means honesty; a drug prescribed to bring out honesty is a serum used in interrogation

explanation.surface: A doctor writes out a prescription for a patient named Verity.
explanation.walkthrough: Verity is a girl's name but also the word for truthfulness.
explanation.definitionFit: A substance such as sodium thiopental supposedly makes a subject speak honestly under questioning.

clue.text: Work on furnishings before magistrate takes case

parts.note: to be up before the beak is to appear in court
a holster is a case for a gun

explanation.surface: A decorator works on soft furnishings before a magistrate hears a case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up before the magistrate' is British idiom for appearing in court.
explanation.definitionFit: To pad and cover chairs and sofas with fabric is to work on furnishings.

clue.text: Cut demand to keep variable stock

parts.note: hack means cut roughly

indicators.note: the word for demand holds the algebra letter inside

parts.note: a need is a demand or requirement
Y is a typical algebraic variable

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper cuts demand so as to retain fluctuating stock.
explanation.walkthrough: Stock looks like a noun for goods but is an adjective, as in a stock phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Overused and trite, like a stock phrase, describes something clichéd.

clue.text: Clever comment pedant keeps back

indicators.note: the run found inside is read in the other direction
the two words hold the letters within them

explanation.surface: A smart remark is held back by a fussy pedant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeps' signals a run hidden across the end of comment and the start of pedant; 'back' turns TPEDA round.
explanation.definitionFit: Being skilled and proficient at something is to be clever at it.

clue.text: Also have wine, as discussed, when needed

indicators.note: discussed means spoken, so the phrase is pronounced rather than spelt

parts.note: to add hock is to also have a German white wine

explanation.surface: A diner agrees to have some wine as well, as previously talked about.
explanation.walkthrough: Hock is a German white wine from the Rhine; 'add hock' is pronounced like the Latin phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A Latin phrase for arrangements made for a particular purpose as the need arises.

clue.text: American soft fruit is exhibited

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical marking for soft
pears are a fruit

explanation.surface: Some soft American fruit is put on show.
explanation.definitionFit: To come into view or be on display is to be exhibited or shown.

clue.text: Lucky escape: electrician finally making circuit safe

indicators.note: only the closing letter of electrician is taken

parts.note: connecting a circuit to the ground is called earthing in Britain

explanation.surface: An electrician grounds a circuit just in time to avoid a shock.
explanation.walkthrough: Earthing is the British word for what Americans call grounding a circuit.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow miss or close call is a situation that almost ended in disaster.

clue.text: Arctic swimmer raced northward with Prince Harry

indicators.note: in a down clue, going northward means reading upwards

parts.note: ran means raced
Prince Hal is Shakespeare's young Henry V

explanation.surface: A swimmer races north alongside Prince Harry.
explanation.walkthrough: Hal is the nickname of the future Henry V in Shakespeare's Henry IV plays.
explanation.definitionFit: This tusked whale lives in Arctic waters, so it is a swimmer of the far north.

clue.text: An eminent Florentine's unhurried pace?

parts.note: Dante Alighieri, the poet, was born in Florence

explanation.surface: A famous Florentine walks at a leisurely pace.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical tempo marking meaning at a walking speed, moderately slow.

clue.text: Good skill involves men producing item worn

indicators.note: the word for skill wraps round the men

parts.note: art means skill, as in the art of persuasion

explanation.surface: Good craftsmanship by men results in something to wear.
explanation.definitionFit: Any piece of clothing is an article of dress that someone puts on.

clue.text: Drunken peril holding tin: it's lager!

indicators.note: the clue word that signals this step
a drunken word staggers into a new order

parts.note: Sn is the chemical symbol for tin

explanation.surface: A drinker staggers about holding a can of lager.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' puts SN inside PILER, the anagram of peril.
explanation.definitionFit: A pale Czech-style beer is a type of lager, named after the town of Plzen.

clue.text: Goddess! Stop luring me in!

indicators.note: the word for stop draws the pronoun inside it
the pronoun ends up within the other word

parts.note: to deter is to stop or discourage

explanation.surface: Someone cries out to a goddess not to seduce them.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek deity of the harvest and grain, mother of Persephone, is a goddess.

clue.text: Some salami served for cheapskate

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A stingy host serves only a little salami.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'for cheapskate' as the definition; 'for' is a link word, and the definition is just 'cheapskate'.
explanation.definitionFit: A stingy person who hoards money and hates spending it is a skinflint.

clue.text: Occasionally ignored threat of French business

indicators.note: every other letter of threat is passed over, keeping the rest

parts.note: de is French for of

explanation.surface: A business sometimes ignores a threat from the French.
explanation.definitionFit: Commerce, buying and selling goods, is business in general.

clue.text: Anxious worker safely evacuated

parts.note: a worker ant is a crossword staple

indicators.note: emptied of its inside letters, leaving only the outer two

explanation.surface: A nervous employee is safely moved out of a building.
explanation.definitionFit: Fidgety and nervous, someone restless is informally said to have ants in their pants.

clue.text: Crewmen given fish: this seals deal

parts.note: deckhands, the members of a ship's crew
hake is a fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: A ship's crew is handed fish to close a bargain.
explanation.definitionFit: Clasping and shaking palms is the customary gesture that confirms an agreement.

clue.text: Pastry one very good, coarse and large

parts.note: a saint is a very good person, abbreviated ST
rude means crude or vulgar
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A pastry is described as excellent, rough-textured and big.
explanation.definitionFit: An Austrian dessert of thin layered dough rolled round apple is a kind of pastry.

clue.text: Republican in Senate unusually sincere

indicators.note: the party letter goes inside the rearranged chamber
unusually means the letters of Senate are arranged differently

explanation.surface: A Republican senator speaks with unusual sincerity in the chamber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' rearranges SENATE to EANEST, with R placed inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Serious and heartfelt, someone genuine in intent is said to be in deadly earnest.
